candidates.structural_interaction: Earth generating Metal cross-polarity — precision that structurally exceeds its container
candidates.k2_overview: Your Metal moves as the Virtuoso: an edge that performs. You cut with style, argue like a fencing match, and produce work so sharp it draws blood and applause in the same stroke. Standards bore you unless you set them. Authority irritates you unless it earned itself. The world calls it attitude. It is precision refusing dullness.
candidates.k2_functional: Your wit cuts clean and quotable. People fear your reviews and collect them.

k2_domain_readings.Talent: Your talent is the brilliant edge: work with finish other people cannot reach. Sign it, show it, price it properly. Metal brilliance that stays sheathed reads as arrogance without the receipts.
k2_domain_readings.Performance: You perform with precision: the flawless delivery, the duel won in public. Choose stages where exactness shines, competitions, critiques, crafts. Applause for sharpness is the kind you can actually live on.
k2_domain_readings.Defiance: Your defiance is the refusal to dull: standards no supervisor can lower, corners you will not round. Aim it at shoddiness rather than at every hand holding a clipboard. Rebellion with a portfolio wins.

catalyst.define: As a catalyst, little leaves the gate and what does come out is sharp. Your finest work waits for a moment with an audience.

angles.drive: Saying it straight is the only way you know. A softened truth feels like a lie with manners to you, and you name what is wrong ahead of smoothing it over. Whoever asks your view walks away with the real one.
angles.cost_self: Being straight costs you the welcome. Because being right out loud matters more than comfort to you, you say the unsaid thing and lose a few invitations. What you want is a circle where honesty counts as a kindness.
angles.cost_others: Whenever something is wrong, you say so before you say anything kind. Being exact feels more honest to you than being gentle, and you hand people the mistake ahead of the credit. Your praise reaches them late, after the sting has landed.

angles.drive: Setting the bar is something you do unasked. A standard you did not choose bores you, so you set your own rather than keep the given one, and hold yourself to it. What leaves your hands has already passed the hardest judge it will meet.
angles.cost_self: You never rest under a bar you set yourself. Because the standard is yours, you raise it rather than meet it, and the mark moves each time you near it. Your wins go by uncelebrated, since none of them was ever the goal.
angles.cost_others: When you set the bar, you set it for everyone near you. Your standard feels more honest than a shared one, and you hold the people beside you to a mark they never chose. Some do their finest work because you asked for it.

angles.drive: Being watched brings out your best work. A thing done unseen feels half real to you, and you perform with someone watching rather than practice alone. Anyone in the seats gets years of your craft in a single hour.
angles.cost_self: Your best needs a witness. With no one there to rise for, you let the private hours go slack rather than drill them, and the talent that grows unseen stays small. Applause is what you are after, and an empty hall gives none.
angles.cost_others: You save your best for an audience. A crowd feels more worth rising for than one person, and you perform for strangers ahead of the people at home. Your own household gets you after the show, the shine already spent.

friction.define: As a friction, the gate stays wide open, since being exact is how you feel safe. Your edge comes out ahead of your warmth, and closeness pays for it.

angles.drive: Direct is the only setting you have for the truth. A softened answer feels like a lie you would have to keep up, so you say it exactly rather than gently. You only ever wanted to be believed, and the hurt was never the point.
angles.cost_self: Direct talk costs you people who would have stayed. Being right counts for more with you than a welcome, so you say the hard thing and lose easy company. You lose the company you came for each time you say it that directly.
angles.cost_others: You hand people your read in its plainest, most direct form. Plain truth feels like respect to you, so you skip the soft words rather than soften the point. You leave them a bruise the truth alone would not have left.

angles.drive: Talking back comes first in you. A rule you did not agree to feels like being pushed around, so you talk back rather than ask what it is for. You spend your talking back on small rules and have none left for big ones.
angles.cost_self: You talk back hardest to the people who correct you. Because being corrected feels like being made small, you talk back to whoever could teach you instead of learning from them. You win the back-and-forth and leave the lesson behind.
angles.cost_others: Given a task by a teacher, you talk back first. Since the last word guards your pride, you would rather talk back than get on with it. You use up a little of their patience with every small fight.

angles.drive: Grading people is something you do without meaning to. A quick read of someone's worth feels safer than not knowing, so you grade them on sight rather than wait to be surprised. Remember that you owe no one a grade on first sight.
angles.cost_self: Grading someone costs you what they know. Since you would rather be right about a person than learn from them, you stop listening at the grade. You learn almost nothing from a person once you have graded them.
angles.cost_others: When you meet someone, you grade them before you greet them. The fast read feels more honest than the slow one, and you give people the grade instead of your attention. You rarely let anyone change the first grade you gave them.

edge.lead: Metal runs through your mind, your career and your social life. It is the question that lets the air out of a bad idea, the show you build for a full hall and open when ready, and the line at dinner quoted for years.
